skill.name: documentation-templates
skill.description: Provides reusable structures for README files, API references, code comments, changelogs, architecture decisions, and AI-friendly project documentation.
skill.summary: Create consistent project documentation with practical templates and structure guidelines.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Inconsistent documentation makes projects difficult to understand and maintain. This skill provides adaptable templates for common technical documentation.
actual_capabilities: Structures README files with prioritized sections for setup, features, configuration, references, and licensing.
Provides a per-endpoint API documentation template with parameters, responses, and examples.
Supplies JSDoc and TSDoc guidance for parameters, returns, errors, and usage examples.
Creates starter structures for changelogs and architecture decision records.
Organizes llms.txt and retrieval-friendly documentation with clear hierarchies and self-contained sections.
limitations: The skill does not inspect a repository or generate project-specific facts automatically.
Every template contains placeholders that require manual adaptation.
The skill does not validate API behavior, code correctness, or documentation accuracy.
It provides guidance only and includes no publishing or formatting automation.

use_cases.title: Launch a Project README
use_cases.description: Build a concise README that helps contributors install, configure, and understand a new project.

use_cases.title: Standardize API References
use_cases.description: Apply one endpoint structure across parameters, responses, errors, and examples.

use_cases.title: Record Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Capture decision context, status, consequences, and tradeoffs in a repeatable format.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic README
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README for [project]. Include a one-line purpose, quick start, key features, configuration, documentation links, and license.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting documentation for a small project

prompt_templates.title: Document an API Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Document [method and path]. Describe its purpose, parameters, successful response, common errors, and one realistic request and response example.
prompt_templates.scenario: Adding one endpoint to an API reference

prompt_templates.title: Write an Architecture Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an ADR for [decision]. Explain the context, chosen option, rejected alternatives, current status, consequences, and known tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design an AI-Friendly Documentation Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design documentation for [project] that supports people and retrieval systems. Include navigation, self-contained sections, an llms.txt outline, key concepts, and update ownership.
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning documentation for human readers and AI retrieval

output_examples.input: Create a README outline for a command-line log analyzer.
output_examples.output: A structured outline covering purpose, installation, quick start, commands, configuration, usage examples, troubleshooting, contributing, and license.

output_examples.input: Document the endpoint that retrieves an account by identifier.
output_examples.output: An endpoint reference with purpose, identifier requirements, success behavior, not-found behavior, and representative request and response descriptions.

output_examples.input: Record the decision to use PostgreSQL instead of SQLite.
output_examples.output: An ADR describing scalability needs, the accepted PostgreSQL choice, considered alternatives, migration costs, operational requirements, and expected benefits.

best_practices: Replace every placeholder with verified project information before publishing.
Keep examples realistic and update them when behavior changes.
Organize content from quick answers to detailed references.
anti_patterns: Do not publish a template with unresolved placeholder text.
Do not document behavior that has not been verified against the project.
Do not repeat the same details across several files without clear ownership.

faq.question: Which documentation types are included?
faq.answer: The skill covers README files, API endpoints, code comments, changelogs, architecture decisions, llms.txt, and retrieval-friendly structures.

faq.question: Does the skill generate documentation from source code?
faq.answer: No. It provides structures and guidance, but project facts must be supplied and verified.

faq.question: Can I adapt the templates to an existing documentation standard?
faq.answer: Yes. Adjust headings, terminology, depth, and examples while preserving the required information.

faq.question: Does it support API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. The endpoint template covers purpose, parameters, response states, and examples.

faq.question: How does it support AI-friendly documentation?
faq.answer: It recommends clear heading hierarchies, self-contained sections, structured examples, diagrams, and an llms.txt overview.

faq.question: Should generated documentation be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Verify all commands, interfaces, defaults, links, and examples against the current project.
